sections.title: Common Roots Between Two Quadratics
sections.content: If a1x² + b1x + c1 = 0 and a2x² + b2x + c2 = 0 have both roots common, then a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2. If only one root is common, use cross-multiplication.

sections.title: Newton's Sums (Theory of Equations)
sections.content: If α, β are roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 and Sn = α^n + β^n (or α^n - β^n), then a(Sn) + b(Sn-1) + c(Sn-2) = 0.

sections.title: Method of Differences (Telescoping Series)
sections.content: Express the general term Tn as the difference of two consecutive terms, Vn - Vn-1. When summed from 1 to N, all intermediate terms cancel out.

sections.title: Resolution into Two Linear Factors
sections.content: A general 2nd-degree equation ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 can be factored into two linear equations if its determinant Δ (abc + 2fgh - af² - bg² - ch²) equals 0.

sections.title: Advanced Inequalities
sections.content: Using Weighted AM-GM, Cauchy-Schwarz, or Holder's inequality to find bounds (minimum/maximum values) of complex multi-variable sequence expressions.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Misidentifying the telescoping pattern or missing terms that don't cancel.
2) Assuming both roots are common when only one is.
3) Messing up indices (n, n-1, n-2) in Newton's formula.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 tackles high-level JEE Advanced concepts: recursive root relations (Newton's), cancellation in complex series, and multivariable quadratic conditions.

tricks.title: One Common Root Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Solve the two quadratics by cross-multiplication to establish the condition for the common root α.

tricks.title: Newton's Formula Trick
tricks.explanation: Quickly find sums of high powers of roots without ever calculating the individual roots.

tricks.title: Telescoping Fraction Trick
tricks.explanation: Split denominator products into partial fractions to force term cancellation.

tricks.title: Sum of Squares/Cubes Series
tricks.explanation: Memorize these identities to substitute directly inside larger, complex summations.
